description: NEBULON is a team driven by curiosity, creativity, and a passion for space exploration and technology. We combine research, data analysis, software, and design to create an interactive platform for exploring terrestrial analog locations. Our project focuses on identifying Earth locations that share environmental, geological, and terrain characteristics with the Moon or Mars. Using NASA and open-source data, we aim to make complex planetary information easier to explore and understand. Through our platform, users can discover potential analog sites, explore their characteristics, and understand their relevance to future lunar and planetary exploration.
summary: Project Nebulon is a web-based platform developed to explore and document human-made objects abandoned on the Moon and Mars during space exploration missions. It aims to bring information about these objects together in one accessible digital space, helping users discover the history of space missions and the equipment left behind. Our project addresses NASA's "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge by highlighting the forgotten remains of human exploration beyond Earth. Through a simple and user-friendly website, users can explore information about artificial objects and understand their connection to past space missions. Project Nebulon helps preserve space exploration history, promotes awareness of planetary heritage, and makes space-related information easier to access and understand.
details:
0:00 – 0:30 | The Vision: Bringing Silent Monuments to Life

"Since the 1960s, NASA has left dozens of pioneering rovers, landers, impactors, and probes across the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Usually, their history is locked away in dry coordinate tables and textbooks. We built Deep Space Archivist—an interactive, browser-based 3D Mission Control Tracking Station designed for space enthusiasts aged 10 to 16. Instead of just reading about space history, users step into the role of a flight director to track real NASA hardware, trace their interplanetary journeys, and read first-person stories told from the perspective of the machines themselves."

0:30 – 1:15 | Core Features & Live Demo Flow

"Our application operates as a unified, real-time 3D solar system:

Live Orbital Mechanics & Time Warp: Users can view the heliocentric solar system with visible planetary orbits and interactive time-warp controls that accelerate planetary motion from real time up to 1,000x speed.

Precision Surface Mapping: Clicking on the Moon or Mars flies the camera directly to the planet's surface, where glowing telemetry beacons mark the exact NASA landing coordinates of artifacts like the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Surveyor 3, and the Opportunity Rover.

End-to-End Trajectory Replay: When a user activates the Guided Tour on any mission, the engine dynamically draws a 3D transfer trajectory from launch at Cape Canaveral on Earth, across interplanetary space, right down to the exact crater where the craft completed its mission and was abandoned.

Interactive Dossiers & Live Audio Telemetry: Selecting any vessel opens a mission-control dossier breaking down its narrative, hardware, and scientific discoveries, complete with a live 'Ping Signal' feature that synthesizes distinct acoustic returns for silent monuments versus active laser retroreflectors."

1:15 – 2:00 | How We Built It (Engineering & Tech Stack)

"We engineered the platform from the ground up in Visual Studio Code with a focus on zero-lag browser performance:

Frontend & Tooling: We scaffolded the application with React and Vite for fast hot-module replacement and optimized builds, using Tailwind CSS to construct a non-blocking heads-up display over the 3D canvas.

3D Rendering & Coordinate Math: Using Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Drei, we wrote custom spherical-to-Cartesian trigonometric functions and surface-normal quaternions to convert NASA's latitude and longitude data into 3D vectors, alongside 3D Catmull-Rom splines for the Earth-to-target trajectory arcs.

Procedural Asset Generation: Rather than bogging down the browser with heavy external downloads, we used the HTML5 Canvas API to procedurally generate planetary surface textures and the native Web Audio API to synthesize real-time oscillator telemetry pings—making the entire web app lightweight and instantly deployable to Vercel and Firebase Hosting."
